card.title: Specific vs latent heat — warming vs changing phase

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Specific heat capacity (c) is the heat per kilogram per kelvin to WARM a substance — temperature rises. Latent heat (L) is the heat per kilogram to CHANGE PHASE at constant temperature — bonds break, thermometer stalls. Newton's law of cooling (rate ∝ excess temperature) governs the approach to room temperature. The triple point is the unique (P, T) where solid, liquid and vapour coexist.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: sensible: Q = m·c·ΔT (c in J·kg⁻¹·K⁻¹)  ·  phase change: Q = m·L (fusion L_f, vaporization L_v)  ·  calorimetry: heat lost = heat gained  ·  cooling: dT/dt = −k(T − T₀)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Q = mcΔT needs no phase change in the interval and roughly constant c. Latent formulas need constant pressure and the pure substance at its transition point. Newton's law holds for small excess temperatures with convection-dominated loss. Mixture-method calorimetry assumes an isolated (no-loss) calorimeter.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Water's c = 4200 J/kg·K (huge — climate buffer); ice L_f = 3.34×10⁵ J/kg, steam L_v = 2.26×10⁶ J/kg (burns scald worse than boiling water at the same T). Aluminium block 200 g, 20→100 °C: Q = 0.2 × 900 × 80 = 14,400 J (NEB 2024 pattern).

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: 200 g aluminium, 20 °C → 100 °C, c = 900 J/kg·K: Q = mcΔT = 0.2 × 900 × 80 = 14,400 J absorbed (NEB 2024, 3 marks). Same template with L answers 'how much ice melts' questions — just swap mcΔT for mL and hold T fixed.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: c is not truly constant (rises with T; Dulong–Petit explains solids). Latent heat vanishes at the critical point (no phase boundary left). Newton's law fails for large ΔT (radiation ∝ T⁴ takes over) and forced convection.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Mixture method: hot solid (m₁, c₁, T₁) into water (m₂, c₂, T₂) reaching T: m₁c₁(T₁−T) = m₂c₂(T−T₂) + calorimeter term → solve for the unknown c. Latent-heat measurement runs the same ledger with one side as mL. Cooling law integrates to exponential decay T − T₀ = (Tᵢ−T₀)e^(−kt).

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: 'Heats / cools / mixes' → write the heat-lost = heat-gained ledger first. 'Melts / boils / condenses' → mL with NO ΔT. Triple point = one sentence (all three phases coexist). Units check: c in J/kg·K, L in J/kg.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB 2024 (3): specific heat capacity + 200 g aluminium 20→100 °C numerical. NEB 2023 (3): latent heat — fusion vs vaporization. NEB 2023 (3): Q and c definitions + heat-to-raise-temperature formula.
